guide_enrichment.narrative:
We see a clear path for Texas to create separation through the air. Our numbers rate the Texas passing offense much more favorably than UT San Antonio’s pass defense, and the opener showed the available explosiveness: Texas generated 516 yards at 7.0 yards per play, while Arch Manning threw for 305 yards and four touchdowns. That is useful context, not proof that the same production carries over automatically.

The concern for us is whether Texas consistently turns that advantage into enough scoring opportunities to cover a large number. Our metrics are less enthusiastic about Texas’ ability to create those opportunities, while UT San Antonio’s passing offense also has a plausible matchup against the Texas pass defense. Texas forced three turnovers in its opener, but takeaways can amplify a margin in ways we do not want to assume will repeat.

That leaves our overall expectation essentially aligned with the market. We understand the case for a comfortable Texas win, but the current price already accounts for much of the passing mismatch. For us, there is not enough separation between our view and the market to justify a wager.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Texas’ receivers against the UT San Antonio pass defense. Ryan Wingo caught seven passes for 121 yards and a touchdown in the opener, while Cam Coleman added 70 yards and two touchdowns on three catches. That combination gives Manning multiple ways to generate explosive plays, which is the clearest route to Texas building margin.

The question is whether those passing gains produce sustained scoring rather than isolated highlights. That conversion will matter more to our view than the final yardage total alone.

recent_game.fact: Texas opened the 2026 season with a 59-7 home win over Texas State on Sept. 5.
Texas produced 516 total yards and averaged 7.0 yards per play against Texas State.
Texas' running backs accounted for 156 rushing yards and three touchdowns against Texas State.
Texas forced three turnovers—two fumbles and one interception—against Texas State.

opponent_notes.fact: Texas defeated UTSA 41-20 in 2022 and 56-7 in 2024; both games were played in Austin.
Arch Manning produced a 75-yard touchdown pass and a 67-yard touchdown run against UTSA in 2024.
Manning accounted for five touchdowns—four passing and one rushing—against UTSA in 2024 after replacing an injured Quinn Ewers.

quarterback.fact: Senior quarterback Arch Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns in the 2026 opener against Texas State.
Manning is 13-3 as a starter and 9-0 as a starter at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium.
In 2025, Manning completed 248 of 404 passes for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns while adding 399 rushing yards and a team-high 10 rushing touchdowns.
Texas added quarterback MJ Morris from Coastal Carolina through the transfer portal for 2026.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running backs Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers transferred to Texas in spring 2026 from Arizona State and NC State, respectively.
Smothers recorded 72 rushing yards on 10 attempts and caught three passes for 28 yards and a touchdown against Texas State, totaling 100 yards from scrimmage.
Brown had 11 carries for 34 yards and two touchdowns plus one reception for 11 yards in his Texas debut.
Wide receiver Ryan Wingo caught seven passes for 121 yards and one touchdown against Texas State.
Transfer wide receiver Cam Coleman caught three passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns in his Texas debut against Texas State.
Texas returns 2025 offensive-line starters Trevor Goosby, Brandon Baker, Cole Hutson and Connor Robertson.
Texas added offensive linemen Laurence Seymore III, Melvin Siani and Dylan Sikorski through the transfer portal.
Texas added tight end Michael Masunas from Michigan State; he had 19 receptions for 232 yards and three touchdowns in 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: EDGE Colin Simmons led Texas in 2025 with 15.5 tackles for loss, 12 sacks, 15 pressures, three forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.
Simmons opened 2026 with one tackle, a half tackle for loss, one quarterback hurry and a fumble recovery against Texas State.
Texas added linebackers Rasheem Biles, Markus Boswell, Justin Cryer and Darius Snow through the transfer portal for 2026.
Texas added defensive backs Nick Hudson and Bo Mascoe and defensive linemen Ian Geffrard and Zion Williams through the transfer portal.

coaching_changes.fact: Will Muschamp is Texas' defensive coordinator, with Johnny Nansen serving as co-defensive coordinator and linebackers coach.
Kyle Flood is Texas' offensive coordinator and offensive-line coach, while AJ Milwee is co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
Jeff Banks serves as assistant head coach, special-teams coordinator and tight ends coach.

offensive_context.fact: Texas did not punt in its 59-7 win over Texas State, its first game without a punt since playing Kansas in 2023.
Texas entered the Ohio State game ranked third nationally in total offense at 671.0 yards per game and third in passing offense at 434.0 yards per game after one game.
Texas has won 19 consecutive games when winning time of possession.

defensive_context.fact: Texas has forced a turnover in 24 consecutive home games, the longest active streak in the FBS.
Texas has forced at least one turnover in 36 of its last 37 games.
Texas recorded 21 takeaways in 2025, leading the SEC, and its 16 interceptions ranked second in the conference.
Texas recorded at least 40 sacks and 15 interceptions in both 2024 and 2025.

special_teams.fact: Texas added punter Mac Chiumento from Florida State, kicker Gianni Spetic from Memphis and deep snapper Trey Dubuc from New Mexico for 2026.

series_context.fact: The 2026 matchup will be the third meeting between Texas and UTSA, with Texas winning each of the first two games in Austin.

other_relevant.fact: Thirty-three players made their Texas debuts in the 59-7 season-opening win over Texas State.
Texas added 22 players through the transfer portal for the 2026 season.
Texas has won 21 consecutive home games against unranked opponents and is 21-1 in its last 22 games at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium.
